documents.titleEn: Harmonic oscillator: Verlet phase error and energy | Runnable example
documents.text: 固定入力から実行・検証 調和振動子：Verletの位相誤差とエネルギー Verlet軌道を解析的な振動と比べ、状態誤差・元のエネルギーの偏差・時間反転を確認する。 既存の単位質量・単位角振動数の調和振動子をvelocity Verletで進める。20時間単位、200/400/800刻みの解析解比較、元のエネルギー偏差、時間反転を出力。 式・図・誤差の解説 · 対応するコードZIP 前提H=(q²+p²)/2、(q₀,p₀)=(1,0.2)。固定刻み、非散逸1自由度。初期値・終端時刻・刻み数は入力に明記。最大刻みh=0.1はhω<2の安定域。単位無次元化し質量m=1・角振動数ω=1。pはこの規約の正準運動量、エネルギーは(q²+p²)/2。境界・モデルの範囲時間初期値問題。空間境界なし。出力時刻0〜20の両端を含む。 入力と実行 固定入力 / recipes/harmonic-oscillator.json 実行する場所：atlas-code-2026-11-22（ZIPを展開した中の配布版フォルダ） python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python run_recipe.py --input recipes/harmonic-oscillator.json --output output-harmonic-oscillatorテストと依存関係のファイルpython -m pytest -q tests/test_recipes.py core / requirements.txt testing / requirements.txt plotting / requirements.txt 出力・検証条件・引用を確認する できるファイルと参照出力 result.json (JSON) · 配布版の参照出力 solution.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 参照の種類と比較方法 CSVは最細刻みの時刻ごとに数値・解析のq,pとエネルギーを整列。観測次数は終端状態誤差から、エネルギー偏差は全保存時刻から計算。 同梱された参照出力の代表値 固定入力の参照出力から表示しています。有限格子の値と解析解・独立参照を区別し、再実行の判定には下の許容誤差表を使います。 final_state_error0.000480840593162max_state_error0.000512324125997minimum_observed_order2.00033895323max_relative_energy_deviation0.000150240304723reversal_error5.97873396028e-16final_time_error0 期待する値と許容誤差 表はこの例で採用する数値検査の条件です。参照値との一致だけで、全ての条件や原論文の全結果を再現したという意味にはなりません。横長の表は左右にスクロールできます。 確認する量参照値・許容誤差結果JSON内の場所 全時刻の位相空間誤差を解析解と比較。value ≤ 0.001/metrics/max_state_error 終端状態誤差の観測次数が2次に整合。value ≥ 1.9/metrics/minimum_observed_order 元のHamiltonianの相対偏差を有限区間で測る。厳密保存とは呼ばない。value ≤ 0.0002/metrics/max_relative_energy_deviation 固定刻みを逆向きに戻した状態差。value ≤ 1e-11/metrics/reversal_error 指定した終端時刻に到達。value ≤ 1e-14/metrics/final_time_error 全数値条件の判定all values = true/checks 実行した固定入力のSHA-256value = b498106a876b71e8d6d3444c57b4e6cea0fd2a000d786a5ab3b91ec64804f4b4/input_sha256 入力に記載した条件の合格value = true/passed 失敗・未収束と確認の限界 hω≥2、非有限入力、不明な方式・系、倍増でない刻み一覧を拒否。反転が良くても長時間位相誤差や元のHamiltonianの厳密保存を保証しない。非線形振動子・多体系への検証ではない。 引用・出典と利用条件 Hiroshi Koyama, 調和振動子：Verletの位相誤差とエネルギー, version 2026-11-22. https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/code-and-data/?lang=en#harmonic-oscillator-en 計算に使った設定・変更・ハッシュ・参照日を追記してください。手法を研究に使うときは、以下の原論文も確認し引用します。 CSVは最細刻みの時刻ごとに数値・解析のq,pとエネルギーを整列。観測次数は終端状態誤差から、エネルギー偏差は全保存時刻から計算。 独立な解析式q=q₀cos t+p₀sin t、p=−q₀sin t+p₀cos t。数値解の細格子値を厳密解とは呼ばない。 既存のVerlet手法項目の文献。今回の実行で原論文の全計算を再現するわけではない。 自作実装コード：MIT · 本文・図・データの条件 自作コードはMIT。入力・数値データ・図・本文はサイトの個別条件に従います。この台帳は利用許諾を拡大しません。 版とSHA-256を確認するEditionnumerical-methods-atlas / 2026-11-22ZIP SHA-25615c8c9c26cebc37b1e0c2923f91db456f8c9d157a48618f154f4b9bb39010fd7Input SHA-256b498106a876b71e8d6d3444c57b4e6cea0fd2a000d786a5ab3b91ec64804f4b4 ファイル目録 / Manifest · 配布版の検証記録 公開ファイルからの確認 この例の再実行：合格 入力・環境・時間・合否の記録 / JSON 数値判定はこの固定条件を対象とします。原子2例は同じ1回の実行を共有します。 FIXED INPUT · EXECUTION · VALIDATION Harmonic oscillator: Verlet phase error and energy Compare Verlet trajectories with analytic oscillation; inspect state error, original-energy deviation and time reversal. Advance the existing unit-mass, unit-frequency harmonic oscillator with velocity Verlet. Compare analytic states over 20 time units at 200/400/800 steps, original-energy deviation and reversal. Equations, figures and error analysis · Code ZIP for this example AssumptionsH=(q²+p²)/2 and (q0,p0)=(1,0.2); one nondissipative degree of freedom, fixed steps. Inputs explicitly provide initial state, final time and counts. Largest h=0.1 lies in h*omega<2.UnitsNondimensional unit mass m=1 and angular frequency omega=1; p is canonical momentum and energy is (q²+p²)/2.Boundaries and model scopeTemporal initial-value problem with no spatial boundary; output includes times 0 and 20. Inputs and execution Fixed input / recipes/harmonic-oscillator.json Run from: atlas-code-2026-11-22 (the edition directory inside the extracted ZIP) python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python run_recipe.py --input recipes/harmonic-oscillator.json --output output-harmonic-oscillatorTests and dependency filespython -m pytest -q tests/test_recipes.py core / requirements.txt testing / requirements.txt plotting / requirements.txt Inspect outputs, acceptance and citation Generated files and reference outputs result.json (JSON) · Packaged reference output solution.csv (CSV) · Packaged reference output Reference type and comparison CSV aligns numerical/analytic q,p and energy on the finest time grid. Observed order uses endpoint-state errors; energy deviation uses all recorded times. Selected values from the packaged reference output Read from the fixed-input reference output. Distinguish finite-grid values from analytic or independently computed references; use the tolerance table below to validate a rerun. final_state_error0.000480840593162max_state_error0.000512324125997minimum_observed_order2.00033895323max_relative_energy_deviation0.000150240304723reversal_error5.97873396028e-16final_time_error0 Expected values and tolerances These are numerical acceptance conditions for this example. Agreement does not establish every condition or reproduce all results of the original papers. Wide tables scroll horizontally. QuantityReference / acceptanceLocation in result JSON Compare phase-space error with the analytic solution over all output times.value ≤ 0.001/metrics/max_state_error Endpoint-error refinement is consistent with second order.value ≥ 1.9/metrics/minimum_observed_order Measure relative deviation of the original Hamiltonian over this finite interval; not exact conservation.value ≤ 0.0002/metrics/max_relative_energy_deviation State difference after reversing the same fixed steps.value ≤ 1e-11/metrics/reversal_error Reach the specified final time.value ≤ 1e-14/metrics/final_time_error All numerical acceptance flagsall values = true/checks SHA-256 of the executed fixed inputvalue = b498106a876b71e8d6d3444c57b4e6cea0fd2a000d786a5ab3b91ec64804f4b4/input_sha256 Acceptance conditions in the input passedvalue = true/passed Failure, nonconvergence and verification limits Reject h*omega>=2, nonfinite inputs, unknown method/system and non-doubling counts. Accurate reversal does not establish long-time phase accuracy or exact original-Hamiltonian conservation. Not validation of nonlinear oscillators or many-body systems. Citation, sources and terms Hiroshi Koyama, Harmonic oscillator: Verlet phase error and energy, version 2026-11-22. https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/code-and-data/?lang=en#harmonic-oscillator-en Add the settings, changes, hashes and access date used in your calculation. When using the method in research, review and cite the original method publications too. CSV aligns numerical/analytic q,p and energy on the finest time grid. Observed order uses endpoint-state errors; energy deviation uses all recorded times. Independent analytic q=q0*cos(t)+p0*sin(t), p=-q0*sin(t)+p0*cos(t); no fine numerical solution is called exact. documents.text: 固定入力から実行・検証 He：閉殻HF・交換のみLDA 球対称1s²のHeをRHFと交換のみLDAで解き、SCF収束・エネルギー・電子数を独立な有限基底参照と照合する。 Heの球対称1s²・閉殻HFとスピン非偏極Dirac交換のみLDAを比較します。電子相関・分子・周期系は含みません。 式・図・誤差の解説 · 対応するコードZIP 前提非相対論・無限質量の点核、2電子が単一1s空間軌道を二重占有。2次中心差分と線形密度混合。HF交換の局所還元はこの2電子問題に限定。単位原子単位系：エネルギーhartree、距離bohr。境界・モデルの範囲球対称の孤立系、u(0)=u(r_max)=0。主計算r_max=16 bohr。格子幅と領域打切りを別々に検査。 入力と実行 固定入力 / inputs.json 実行する場所：quantum-atoms-2026-11-21（ZIPを展開した中の配布版フォルダ） python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt python run.py --input inputs.json --reference reference-pyscf.json --output output --figures このコマンドは水素型原子とHeをまとめて計算します。水素型は核電荷・量子数を指定した1電子問題、Heは2電子・球対称1s²のSCF問題です。HeのHFと交換のみLDAは、電子相関を含む厳密なHeとは異なります。 テストと依存関係のファイルpython -m pytest -q core / requirements.txt testing / requirements-dev.txt plotting / requirements-dev.txt 出力・検証条件・引用を確認する できるファイルと参照出力 results.json (JSON) · 配布版の参照出力 profiles/helium-hf.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 profiles/helium-lda_x.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 同梱された参照出力の代表値 固定入力の参照出力から表示しています。有限格子の値と解析解・独立参照を区別し、再実行の判定には下の許容誤差表を使います。 hf / E finite grid (hartree)-2.86165918206hf / E independent reference (hartree)-2.86167999499lda_x / E finite grid (hartree)-2.72361865878lda_x / E independent reference (hartree)-2.72363979148 期待する値と許容誤差 表はこの例で採用する数値検査の条件です。参照値との一致だけで、全ての条件や原論文の全結果を再現したという意味にはなりません。横長の表は左右にスクロールできます。 確認する量参照値・許容誤差結果JSON内の場所 全格子のSCF収束value = true/helium/refinement · field converged 電子数|value − 2| ≤ 1e-12/helium/refinement · field electron_count 入力出力密度のL1残差value ≤ 1e-09/helium/refinement · field density_residual 出力密度での軌道残差value ≤ 1e-07 hartree/helium/refinement · field orbital_residual エネルギー恒等式の誤差value ≤ 1e-10 hartree/helium/refinement · field energy_identity_error h²外挿と独立参照の差（誤差の保証ではない）|value| ≤ 1e-08 hartree/helium/independent_comparison · field extrapolated_reference_difference 独立参照との密度L1差value ≤ 5e-05/helium/independent_comparison · field radial_density_l1_difference 意図した失敗・未収束の判定 確認する量参照値・許容誤差結果JSON内の場所 最大1反復は未収束と判定value = false/helium/expected_nonconvergence · field converged 終了理由を保存value = max_iterations/helium/expected_nonconvergence · field reason 引用・出典と利用条件 Hiroshi Koyama, He：閉殻HF・交換のみLDA, version 2026-11-21. https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/code-and-data/?lang=en#helium-ground-state-en 計算に使った設定・変更・ハッシュ・参照日を追記してください。手法を研究に使うときは、以下の原論文も確認し引用します。 PySCF 2.11.0 / LibxcのGaussian基底参照。外挿値・有限格子値・参照を区別。参照scriptの再実行は今回の共通runnerの測定に含まない。 原法の文献：Roothaan, C. C. J. (1951), New Developments in Molecular Orbital Theory 原法の文献：Kohn, W.; Sham, L. J. (1965), Self-Consistent Equations Including Exchange and Correlation Effects 原法の文献：Dirac, P. A. M. (1930), Note on Exchange Phenomena in the Thomas Atom 自作実装コード：MIT · 本文・図・データの条件 自作コードはMIT。入力・数値データ・図・本文はサイトの個別条件に従います。この台帳は利用許諾を拡大しません。 版とSHA-256を確認するEditionquantum-atoms / 2026-11-21ZIP SHA-256f81c61b854e68b9750d960a17a133ee9a00ae7bd0c3ee268263caee626cf44c9Input SHA-2568680ad9e5b04b5689b52849c71d849ddb98f9ecc9bea851a0f09d2ee2fcc6237 ファイル目録 / Manifest · 配布版の検証記録 公開ファイルからの確認 この例の再実行：合格 入力・環境・時間・合否の記録 / JSON 数値判定はこの固定条件を対象とします。原子2例は同じ1回の実行を共有します。 FIXED INPUT · EXECUTION · VALIDATION Helium: closed-shell HF and exchange-only LDA Solve spherical 1s² helium with RHF and exchange-only LDA; compare SCF convergence, energies and electron count with independent finite-basis references. Compare spherical 1s² closed-shell helium HF and spin-unpolarized Dirac exchange-only LDA. No electron correlation, molecules or periodic systems. Equations, figures and error analysis · Code ZIP for this example AssumptionsNonrelativistic infinite-mass point nucleus, two electrons doubly occupying a single 1s spatial orbital. Second-order central differences and linear density mixing. Local HF exchange reduction is specific to this two-electron problem.UnitsAtomic units: energy in hartree, distance in bohr.Boundaries and model scopeSpherical isolated system, u(0)=u(r_max)=0. Main domain r_max=16 bohr; mesh and box truncation are studied separately. Inputs and execution Fixed input / inputs.json Run from: quantum-atoms-2026-11-21 (the edition directory inside the extracted ZIP) python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt python run.py --input inputs.json --reference reference-pyscf.json --output output --figures This command computes both hydrogenic atoms and helium. Hydrogenic states are one-electron problems specified by charge and quantum numbers; helium is a two-electron spherical 1s² SCF problem. HF and exchange-only LDA are not exact correlated helium. documents.text: 固定入力から実行・検証 水素型原子：解析解と格子収束 Z=1,2の指定された束縛状態について、エネルギー・動径波動関数・格子収束を解析参照と比べる。 孤立した1電子のH・He⁺について、1s・2s・2p・3dのエネルギーと動径軌道を解析解と比較します。多電子原子や分子の直接解法ではありません。 式・図・誤差の解説 · 対応するコードZIP 前提非相対論・無限質量の点核。核電荷Z=1,2。縮約動径軌道を一様格子の2次中心差分で離散化。単位原子単位系：エネルギーhartree、距離bohr。境界・モデルの範囲孤立系、u(0)=u(r_max)=0。主計算r_max=60 bohr。H 1sの領域打切り依存は別に検査。 入力と実行 固定入力 / inputs.json 実行する場所：quantum-atoms-2026-11-21（ZIPを展開した中の配布版フォルダ） python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt python run.py --input inputs.json --reference reference-pyscf.json --output output --figures このコマンドは水素型原子とHeをまとめて計算します。水素型は核電荷・量子数を指定した1電子問題、Heは2電子・球対称1s²のSCF問題です。HeのHFと交換のみLDAは、電子相関を含む厳密なHeとは異なります。 テストと依存関係のファイルpython -m pytest -q core / requirements.txt testing / requirements-dev.txt plotting / requirements-dev.txt 出力・検証条件・引用を確認する できるファイルと参照出力 results.json (JSON) · 配布版の参照出力 profiles/hydrogenic-z1-n1-l0.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 profiles/hydrogenic-z1-n2-l0.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 profiles/hydrogenic-z1-n2-l1.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 profiles/hydrogenic-z1-n3-l2.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 profiles/hydrogenic-z2-n1-l0.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 profiles/hydrogenic-z2-n2-l0.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 profiles/hydrogenic-z2-n2-l1.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 profiles/hydrogenic-z2-n3-l2.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 同梱された参照出力の代表値 固定入力の参照出力から表示しています。有限格子の値と解析解・独立参照を区別し、再実行の判定には下の許容誤差表を使います。 H 1s / E analytic (hartree)-0.5H 1s / E finite grid (hartree)-0.499987500623H 1s / grid step (bohr)0.01 期待する値と許容誤差 表はこの例で採用する数値検査の条件です。参照値との一致だけで、全ての条件や原論文の全結果を再現したという意味にはなりません。横長の表は左右にスクロールできます。 確認する量参照値・許容誤差結果JSON内の場所 動径軌道の規格化|value − 1| ≤ 1e-12/hydrogenic/refinement · field norm 全固有値問題の残差value ≤ 1e-07 hartree/hydrogenic/refinement · field eigen_residual 最細格子の解析解との差value ≤ 0.00021 hartree/hydrogenic/refinement · where {"dr": 0.01} · field energy_error 格子細分による誤差低減value = true/checks/hydrogenic_exact_energy_errors_reduce 引用・出典と利用条件 Hiroshi Koyama, 水素型原子：解析解と格子収束, version 2026-11-21. https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/code-and-data/?lang=en#hydrogenic-atoms-en 計算に使った設定・変更・ハッシュ・参照日を追記してください。手法を研究に使うときは、以下の原論文も確認し引用します。 E_n=−Z²/(2n²)とLaguerre動径解。有限格子の誤差と箱の誤差を分ける。 原法の文献：Schrödinger, E. (1926), Quantisierung als Eigenwertproblem 自作実装コード：MIT · 本文・図・データの条件 自作コードはMIT。入力・数値データ・図・本文はサイトの個別条件に従います。この台帳は利用許諾を拡大しません。 版とSHA-256を確認するEditionquantum-atoms / 2026-11-21ZIP SHA-256f81c61b854e68b9750d960a17a133ee9a00ae7bd0c3ee268263caee626cf44c9Input SHA-2568680ad9e5b04b5689b52849c71d849ddb98f9ecc9bea851a0f09d2ee2fcc6237 ファイル目録 / Manifest · 配布版の検証記録 公開ファイルからの確認 この例の再実行：合格 入力・環境・時間・合否の記録 / JSON 数値判定はこの固定条件を対象とします。原子2例は同じ1回の実行を共有します。 FIXED INPUT · EXECUTION · VALIDATION Hydrogenic atoms: analytic references and grid refinement Compare energy, radial wavefunctions and grid refinement with analytic references for the specified Z=1,2 bound states. Isolated one-electron H and He⁺: compare 1s, 2s, 2p and 3d energies and radial orbitals against analytic solutions. Not a direct many-electron or molecular solver. Equations, figures and error analysis · Code ZIP for this example AssumptionsNonrelativistic infinite-mass point nucleus, Z=1,2. Reduced radial orbitals use second-order central differences on a uniform mesh.UnitsAtomic units: energy in hartree, distance in bohr.Boundaries and model scopeIsolated boundaries, u(0)=u(r_max)=0. Main domain r_max=60 bohr; hydrogen 1s has a separate box-truncation study. Inputs and execution Fixed input / inputs.json Run from: quantum-atoms-2026-11-21 (the edition directory inside the extracted ZIP) python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt python run.py --input inputs.json --reference reference-pyscf.json --output output --figures This command computes both hydrogenic atoms and helium. Hydrogenic states are one-electron problems specified by charge and quantum numbers; helium is a two-electron spherical 1s² SCF problem. HF and exchange-only LDA are not exact correlated helium. Tests and dependency filespython -m pytest -q core / requirements.txt testing / requirements-dev.txt plotting / requirements-dev.txt Inspect outputs, acceptance and citation Generated files and reference outputs results.json (JSON) · Packaged reference output profiles/hydrogenic-z1-n1-l0.csv (CSV) · Packaged reference output profiles/hydrogenic-z1-n2-l0.csv (CSV) · Packaged reference output profiles/hydrogenic-z1-n2-l1.csv (CSV) · Packaged reference output profiles/hydrogenic-z1-n3-l2.csv (CSV) · Packaged reference output profiles/hydrogenic-z2-n1-l0.csv (CSV) · Packaged reference output profiles/hydrogenic-z2-n2-l0.csv (CSV) · Packaged reference output profiles/hydrogenic-z2-n2-l1.csv (CSV) · Packaged reference output profiles/hydrogenic-z2-n3-l2.csv (CSV) · Packaged reference output Selected values from the packaged reference output Read from the fixed-input reference output. Distinguish finite-grid values from analytic or independently computed references; use the tolerance table below to validate a rerun. H 1s / E analytic (hartree)-0.5H 1s / E finite grid (hartree)-0.499987500623H 1s / grid step (bohr)0.01 Expected values and tolerances These are numerical acceptance conditions for this example. Agreement does not establish every condition or reproduce all results of the original papers. Wide tables scroll horizontally. When using the method in research, review and cite the original method publications too. E_n=−Z²/(2n²) and Laguerre radial solutions, separating finite-grid and finite-box error. documents.title: 周期PM粒子群：質量・内力・格子場 | 実行・検証例
documents.titleEn: Periodic PM particles: mass, internal force and mesh field | Runnable example
documents.text: 固定入力から実行・検証 周期PM粒子群：質量・内力・格子場 固定19粒子のCIC質量・自己力・内力和・周期折返しを調べ、別の正弦密度で格子ポテンシャルと加速度を解析検証する。 入力JSONに保存した19粒子の周期CIC–FFT–CIC計算。質量、内力和、単粒子自己力、整数箱長移動を確認し、別の正弦密度の解析的周期Poisson場と照合。 式・図・誤差の解説 · 対応するコードZIP 前提3次元立方周期箱L=1、G=1、24³格子、正の質量で総和1。座標・質量は全値を入力に保存し、実行時の乱数生成はない。連続k²のFFT逆演算と同じCIC配置・補間を用いる。単位基準長L=1、総質量M=1、G=1。密度はM/L³、ポテンシャルはGM/L、加速度はGM/L²、力はGM²/L²。境界・モデルの範囲3方向周期。∇²φ=4πG(ρ−〈ρ〉)、φ̂(0)=0。偶数格子の各微分軸のNyquist成分を0にする既存実装。孤立境界の直接和とは異なる。 入力と実行 固定入力 / recipes/periodic-particles.json 実行する場所：atlas-code-2026-11-22（ZIPを展開した中の配布版フォルダ） python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python run_recipe.py --input recipes/periodic-particles.json --output output-periodic-particlesテストと依存関係のファイルpython -m pytest -q tests/test_recipes.py core / requirements.txt testing / requirements.txt plotting / requirements.txt 出力・検証条件・引用を確認する できるファイルと参照出力 result.json (JSON) · 配布版の参照出力 solution.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 参照の種類と比較方法 CSVは粒子ごとの座標・質量・加速度・力。正弦密度の独立解析場検査はJSONの集計値に保存。PM格子細分化を粒子力の解析誤差として誤表示しない。 同梱された参照出力の代表値 固定入力の参照出力から表示しています。有限格子の値と解析解・独立参照を区別し、再実行の判定には下の許容誤差表を使います。 mass_relative_error1.11022302463e-16internal_net_force_norm5.75760967484e-16internal_net_force_relative1.70037565829e-16single_particle_self_acceleration3.99680288865e-15periodic_shift_acceleration_max_error4.61852778244e-14periodic_shift_density_relative_error7.73052288874e-15potential_mean_absolute8.22387425648e-18manufactured_potential_max_error3.46944695195e-17 期待する値と許容誤差 表はこの例で採用する数値検査の条件です。参照値との一致だけで、全ての条件や原論文の全結果を再現したという意味にはなりません。横長の表は左右にスクロールできます。 確認する量参照値・許容誤差結果JSON内の場所 CIC格子へ沈着した総質量。value ≤ 1e-13/metrics/mass_relative_error 質量重み付き内力和を力の大きさの総和で規格化。粒子力の精度とは別。value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/internal_net_force_relative 同じCIC配置・補間を使う単粒子の自己加速度。value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/single_particle_self_acceleration 整数箱長の移動で粒子加速度が不変。value ≤ 1e-11/metrics/periodic_shift_acceleration_max_error 整数箱長移動による沈着密度の相対差。value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/periodic_shift_density_relative_error 周期ポテンシャルの平均0の規約。value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/potential_mean_absolute 別に与えた正弦密度の解析的格子ポテンシャルと比較。value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/manufactured_potential_max_error 同じ正弦密度の解析的格子加速度と比較。value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/manufactured_acceleration_max_error 全数値条件の判定all values = true/checks 実行した固定入力のSHA-256value = 9b44288285eb833f8132411dc681ebee4272ff1f6ee041c2a5a35004645c8b9b/input_sha256 入力に記載した条件の合格value = true/passed 失敗・未収束と確認の限界 非正質量、非有限入力、G≠1、不適切な格子・正弦モード、非整数箱長移動を拒否。質量・内力和・自己力の一致だけでは個々の粒子力の精度を保証しない。周期直接和、短距離補正、Ewald・P3M・PME・SPME、粒子時間発展は実装しない。 引用・出典と利用条件 Hiroshi Koyama, 周期PM粒子群：質量・内力・格子場, version 2026-11-22. https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/code-and-data/?lang=en#periodic-particles-en 計算に使った設定・変更・ハッシュ・参照日を追記してください。手法を研究に使うときは、以下の原論文も確認し引用します。 CSVは粒子ごとの座標・質量・加速度・力。正弦密度の独立解析場検査はJSONの集計値に保存。PM格子細分化を粒子力の解析誤差として誤表示しない。 別入力密度ρ=ρ₀+A cos(kx)に対するφ=−4πGA cos(kx)/k²、a_x=−4πGA sin(kx)/k。粒子群の厳密な周期力参照ではない。 既存PM項目の文献。今回のCIC–FFT方式・境界・検査範囲は入力と実装に明示。 自作実装コード：MIT · 本文・図・データの条件 自作コードはMIT。入力・数値データ・図・本文はサイトの個別条件に従います。この台帳は利用許諾を拡大しません。 版とSHA-256を確認するEditionnumerical-methods-atlas / 2026-11-22ZIP SHA-25615c8c9c26cebc37b1e0c2923f91db456f8c9d157a48618f154f4b9bb39010fd7Input SHA-2569b44288285eb833f8132411dc681ebee4272ff1f6ee041c2a5a35004645c8b9b ファイル目録 / Manifest · 配布版の検証記録 公開ファイルからの確認 この例の再実行：合格 入力・環境・時間・合否の記録 / JSON 数値判定はこの固定条件を対象とします。原子2例は同じ1回の実行を共有します。 FIXED INPUT · EXECUTION · VALIDATION Periodic PM particles: mass, internal force and mesh field Inspect CIC mass, self-force, net internal force and wrapping for 19 fixed particles; separately check mesh potential/acceleration for a sinusoidal density. Periodic CIC–FFT–CIC calculation for 19 particles stored explicitly in input JSON. Check mass, net internal force, single-particle self-force and integer-box translation; separately compare a sinusoidal density with analytic periodic Poisson fields. Equations, figures and error analysis · Code ZIP for this example AssumptionsThree-dimensional periodic cube L=1, G=1, 24³ mesh and positive masses summing to one. All positions/masses are stored explicitly; no runtime random generation. Continuum-k² FFT inversion with matched CIC assignment/interpolation.UnitsReference length L=1, mass M=1 and G=1. Density: M/L³; potential: GM/L; acceleration: GM/L²; force: GM²/L².Boundaries and model scopePeriodic in all three axes: Laplacian(phi)=4*pi*G*(rho-mean(rho)), phi_hat(0)=0. Existing implementation zeros the unpaired Nyquist derivative mode along each even-grid axis. This differs from isolated direct-sum boundaries. Inputs and execution Fixed input / recipes/periodic-particles.json Run from: atlas-code-2026-11-22 (the edition directory inside the extracted ZIP) python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python run_recipe.py --input recipes/periodic-particles.json --output output-periodic-particlesTests and dependency filespython -m pytest -q tests/test_recipes.py core / requirements.txt testing / requirements.txt plotting / requirements.txt Inspect outputs, acceptance and citation Generated files and reference outputs result.json (JSON) · Packaged reference output solution.csv (CSV) · Packaged reference output Reference type and comparison CSV stores each particle's coordinates, mass, acceleration and force. Independent sinusoidal-field diagnostics are JSON metrics. No mesh refinement is misrepresented as analytic particle-force error. Selected values from the packaged reference output Read from the fixed-input reference output. Distinguish finite-grid values from analytic or independently computed references; use the tolerance table below to validate a rerun. mass_relative_error1.11022302463e-16internal_net_force_norm5.75760967484e-16internal_net_force_relative1.70037565829e-16single_particle_self_acceleration3.99680288865e-15periodic_shift_acceleration_max_error4.61852778244e-14periodic_shift_density_relative_error7.73052288874e-15potential_mean_absolute8.22387425648e-18manufactured_potential_max_error3.46944695195e-17 Expected values and tolerances These are numerical acceptance conditions for this example. Agreement does not establish every condition or reproduce all results of the original papers. Wide tables scroll horizontally. QuantityReference / acceptanceLocation in result JSON Total mass deposited onto the CIC mesh.value ≤ 1e-13/metrics/mass_relative_error Normalize net internal force by the sum of force magnitudes; separate from particle-force accuracy.value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/internal_net_force_relative Single-particle self-acceleration with matched CIC assignment/interpolation.value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/single_particle_self_acceleration Acceleration is invariant under integer-box translations.value ≤ 1e-11/metrics/periodic_shift_acceleration_max_error Relative deposited-density difference under integer-box translations.value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/periodic_shift_density_relative_error Zero-mean periodic potential gauge.value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/potential_mean_absolute Compare a separate sinusoidal density with its analytic mesh potential.value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/manufactured_potential_max_error Compare the same sinusoidal density with its analytic mesh acceleration.value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/manufactured_acceleration_max_error All numerical acceptance flagsall values = true/checks SHA-256 of the executed fixed inputvalue = 9b44288285eb833f8132411dc681ebee4272ff1f6ee041c2a5a35004645c8b9b/input_sha256 Acceptance conditions in the input passedvalue = true/passed Failure, nonconvergence and verification limits Reject nonpositive masses, nonfinite inputs, G!=1, invalid grids/sinusoidal modes and noninteger box shifts. Mass/net-force/self-force consistency alone does not establish individual particle-force accuracy. No periodic pair-sum reference, short-range correction, Ewald/P3M/PME/SPME or particle evolution. Citation, sources and terms Hiroshi Koyama, Periodic PM particles: mass, internal force and mesh field, version 2026-11-22. https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/code-and-data/?lang=en#periodic-particles-en Add the settings, changes, hashes and access date used in your calculation. When using the method in research, review and cite the original method publications too. CSV stores each particle's coordinates, mass, acceleration and force. Independent sinusoidal-field diagnostics are JSON metrics. No mesh refinement is misrepresented as analytic particle-force error. For separate rho=rho0+A*cos(k*x), phi=-4*pi*G*A*cos(k*x)/k² and ax=-4*pi*G*A*sin(k*x)/k. Not an exact periodic particle-force reference. Existing PM-method reference; this recipe explicitly fixes its CIC–FFT formulation, boundaries and check scope. documents.text: 固定入力から実行・検証 1次元Poisson：Dirichlet正弦解と2次収束 Thomas法の数値解をsin(πx)と比べ、連続解誤差・独立な離散残差・2次格子収束を分けて確認する。 既存Thomas解法で −u''=π²sin(πx) を15/31/63内部点で解き、解析解sin(πx)、独立な差分残差、格子幅半減の次数を別々に確認する。 式・図・誤差の解説 · 対応するコードZIP 前提定係数・一様格子の3点差分。入力で領域、境界、右辺、格子、解法を固定。ピボットなしThomasに適した正定値三重対角行列で、任意の三重対角行列を検証するものではない。単位無次元のx∈[0,1]とu。次元を戻すなら[f]=[u]/L²。離散相対残差は格子体積重みなしのEuclideanノルム比。境界・モデルの範囲u(0)=u(1)=0。CSVには境界2点も含める。 入力と実行 固定入力 / recipes/poisson-1d-dirichlet.json 実行する場所：atlas-code-2026-11-22（ZIPを展開した中の配布版フォルダ） python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python run_recipe.py --input recipes/poisson-1d-dirichlet.json --output output-poisson-1d-dirichletテストと依存関係のファイルpython -m pytest -q tests/test_recipes.py core / requirements.txt testing / requirements.txt plotting / requirements.txt 出力・検証条件・引用を確認する できるファイルと参照出力 result.json (JSON) · 配布版の参照出力 solution.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 参照の種類と比較方法 CSVは最細格子でx・数値解・解析解・誤差を整列。全3格子の誤差と残差、隣接格子間の次数はresult.jsonに保存。Thomasの原報告は既存台帳でも直接確認未済のため、未検証の一次文献を新たに掲げない。 同梱された参照出力の代表値 固定入力の参照出力から表示しています。有限格子の値と解析解・独立参照を区別し、再実行の判定には下の許容誤差表を使います。 finest_linf_error0.000200821809696minimum_observed_order2.00052153382maximum_true_relative_residual5.26166319192e-14boundary_maximum_absolute_value0 期待する値と許容誤差 表はこの例で採用する数値検査の条件です。参照値との一致だけで、全ての条件や原論文の全結果を再現したという意味にはなりません。横長の表は左右にスクロールできます。 確認する量参照値・許容誤差結果JSON内の場所 63内部点の連続解最大誤差。2次差分の主要誤差π²h²/12に余裕を持つ上限。value ≤ 0.0003/metrics/finest_linf_error 格子幅を半減したときの最大誤差の次数が1.9以上。value ≥ 1.9/metrics/minimum_observed_order 独立な差分式で再計算した離散相対残差。離散化誤差とは別の確認。value ≤ 1e-10/metrics/maximum_true_relative_residual 両端の零Dirichlet条件。value ≤ 1e-14/metrics/boundary_maximum_absolute_value 全数値条件の判定all values = true/checks 実行した固定入力のSHA-256value = 07ae06758f60f77ac198fdad6d056cc0026b32005e76ad7d0f2cc3727be24f51/input_sha256 入力に記載した条件の合格value = true/passed 失敗・未収束と確認の限界 非零境界、別の右辺、異なる領域や不正格子を拒否。有限差分の滑らかな単一解の検査で、Robin/Neumann、可変係数、ピボットの一般的安全性を保証しない。 引用・出典と利用条件 Hiroshi Koyama, 1次元Poisson：Dirichlet正弦解と2次収束, version 2026-11-22. https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/code-and-data/?lang=en#poisson-1d-dirichlet-en 計算に使った設定・変更・ハッシュ・参照日を追記してください。手法を研究に使うときは、以下の原論文も確認し引用します。 CSVは最細格子でx・数値解・解析解・誤差を整列。全3格子の誤差と残差、隣接格子間の次数はresult.jsonに保存。Thomasの原報告は既存台帳でも直接確認未済のため、未検証の一次文献を新たに掲げない。 独立にsin(πx)と右辺を評価する。小残差と連続解誤差は分けて報告する。 自作実装コード：MIT · 本文・図・データの条件 second-order grid refinement. Use the existing Thomas kernel for −u''=π²sin(πx) with 15/31/63 interior nodes; separately check analytic sin(πx), a recomputed discrete residual and halving-grid refinement. documents.title: 2次元Poisson：CG・多重格子とP1 FEM | 実行・検証例
documents.titleEn: 2D Poisson: CG, multigrid and P1 FEM | Runnable example
documents.text: 固定入力から実行・検証 2次元Poisson：CG・多重格子とP1 FEM CG・多重格子の同じ差分解とP1有限要素を調べ、FD最大誤差とFEMのL2・H1半ノルム収束を見比べる。 単位正方形のsin(πx)sin(πy)を参照し、CG/MGは15/31/63内部点、P1 FEMは4/8/16分割で細分化。FDの最大誤差と真の残差、FEMの要素内L2誤差とH1半ノルムを独立に評価する。 式・図・誤差の解説 · 対応するコードZIP 前提定係数 −Δu=2π²sin(πx)sin(πy)。CG/MGは同じ五点SPD系を相対許容値1e-11で解く。FEMは既存の連続P1・対角三角形分割・ILU(0)付きGMRES。FEM誤差は別のDuffy写像と8点積Gauss求積で評価する。単位領域長1・uとも無次元。L2は値の面積積分ノルム、H1半ノルムは勾配誤差の面積積分であり、節点最大誤差や単純な配列ノルムと区別する。境界・モデルの範囲正方形[0,1]²の全周でu=0。FEMの組立て残差は内部自由度だけで評価し、境界反力は除く。 入力と実行 固定入力 / recipes/poisson-2d-sine.json 実行する場所：atlas-code-2026-11-22（ZIPを展開した中の配布版フォルダ） python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python run_recipe.py --input recipes/poisson-2d-sine.json --output output-poisson-2d-sineテストと依存関係のファイルpython -m pytest -q tests/test_recipes.py core / requirements.txt testing / requirements.txt plotting / requirements.txt 出力・検証条件・引用を確認する できるファイルと参照出力 result.json (JSON) · 配布版の参照出力 solution.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 参照の種類と比較方法 CSVのmethod_codeは0=CG、1=多重格子、2=P1 FEM。各方式の最細格子と境界点で、同一行座標の解析解を付す。resolutionはFDで内部点数、FEMで三角形分割前の軸方向分割数。 同梱された参照出力の代表値 固定入力の参照出力から表示しています。有限格子の値と解析解・独立参照を区別し、再実行の判定には下の許容誤差表を使います。 fd_finest_cg_linf_error0.000200821809705fd_finest_multigrid_linf_error0.000200821809251fd_minimum_observed_order2.00052153376fd_maximum_true_relative_residual8.22586953086e-12fd_maximum_cg_multigrid_difference5.89217563629e-12fem_finest_l2_error0.00537743500994fem_finest_h1_seminorm_error0.21753633636fem_minimum_l2_order1.90374780859 期待する値と許容誤差 表はこの例で採用する数値検査の条件です。参照値との一致だけで、全ての条件や原論文の全結果を再現したという意味にはなりません。横長の表は左右にスクロールできます。 確認する量参照値・許容誤差結果JSON内の場所 CGの連続解最大誤差。63内部点で正弦モードの2次差分誤差に余裕を持たせる。value ≤ 0.0003/metrics/fd_finest_cg_linf_error 多重格子の連続解最大誤差。CGと同じ離散問題を使う。value ≤ 0.0003/metrics/fd_finest_multigrid_linf_error CGと多重格子の最大誤差がともに2次収束する。value ≥ 1.9/metrics/fd_minimum_observed_order 独立な五点差分で再計算した相対残差。内部停止1e-11より緩い再評価上限。value ≤ 1e-09/metrics/fd_maximum_true_relative_residual 同じ五点差分解を求めるCGと多重格子の一致。連続解参照とは区別する。value ≤ 1e-09/metrics/fd_maximum_cg_multigrid_difference 16分割P1要素の要素内L2誤差。節点最大誤差ではない。value ≤ 0.01/metrics/fem_finest_l2_error 16分割P1要素の勾配誤差のH1半ノルム。L2誤差と分ける。value ≤ 0.3/metrics/fem_finest_h1_seminorm_error 滑らかな解に対するP1のL2誤差の期待次数2を確認する。value ≥ 1.8/metrics/fem_minimum_l2_order 滑らかな解に対するP1のH1半ノルム誤差の期待次数1を確認する。value ≥ 0.9/metrics/fem_minimum_h1_seminorm_order 組立て剛性行列の内部自由度残差。境界行の反力を残差に混ぜない。value ≤ 1e-09/metrics/fem_maximum_interior_true_relative_residual P1要素の全周零Dirichlet条件。value ≤ 1e-12/metrics/fem_boundary_maximum_absolute_value 全数値条件の判定all values = true/checks 実行した固定入力のSHA-256value = e4928dda7da5eb43bbb33c8739be6d8cc28e0bd6bed9ba6635899daad4c1c244/input_sha256 入力に記載した条件の合格value = true/passed 失敗・未収束と確認の限界 非入れ子FD格子、異なる境界や方程式を拒否。滑らかな正弦解の次数確認に限定し、一般領域・特異解・異方性を保証しない。単一固有モードなのでCGの速い終了を速度比較に用いない。FD/FEMの異なる誤差ノルムを直接同列に扱わない。 引用・出典と利用条件 Hiroshi Koyama, 2次元Poisson：CG・多重格子とP1 FEM, version 2026-11-22. https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/code-and-data/?lang=en#poisson-2d-sine-en 計算に使った設定・変更・ハッシュ・参照日を追記してください。手法を研究に使うときは、以下の原論文も確認し引用します。 CSVのmethod_codeは0=CG、1=多重格子、2=P1 FEM。各方式の最細格子と境界点で、同一行座標の解析解を付す。resolutionはFDで内部点数、FEMで三角形分割前の軸方向分割数。 解析解とその勾配を独立に評価する。FEMのL2/H1は要素内求積であり厳密積分との主張ではない。 既存CG項目の一次文献。単一モードの反復数を一般性能とは解釈しない。 既存多重格子項目の文献。本例は固定階層V-cycleに限定。 既存P1要素項目の区分線形変分近似の文献。現コードの全アルゴリズムを原論文へ帰属しない。 自作実装コード：MIT · 本文・図・データの条件 自作コードはMIT。入力・数値データ・図・本文はサイトの個別条件に従います。この台帳は利用許諾を拡大しません。 版とSHA-256を確認するEditionnumerical-methods-atlas / 2026-11-22ZIP 入力・環境・時間・合否の記録 / JSON 数値判定はこの固定条件を対象とします。原子2例は同じ1回の実行を共有します。 FIXED INPUT · EXECUTION · VALIDATION 2D Poisson: CG, multigrid and P1 FEM Inspect CG/multigrid on the same discrete system and P1 FEM, comparing FD maximum error with separate FEM L2/H1-seminorm refinement. Reference sin(πx)sin(πy) on the unit square; refine CG/MG through 15/31/63 interior nodes and P1 FEM through 4/8/16 subdivisions. Independently evaluate FD maximum errors/true residuals and FEM element-interior L2/H1-seminorm errors. Equations, figures and error analysis · Code ZIP for this example AssumptionsConstant-coefficient −Δu=2π²sin(πx)sin(πy). CG/MG solve the same five-point SPD system to relative tolerance 1e-11. FEM uses existing continuous P1, diagonally split triangles and ILU(0)-GMRES. FEM errors use a separate Duffy map and eight-point product Gauss quadrature.UnitsDimensionless unit-length domain and u. L2 integrates value error over area; H1 seminorm integrates gradient error, separately from nodal maximum or plain array norms.Boundaries and model scopeu=0 around [0,1]². FEM assembled residuals use interior degrees of freedom, excluding boundary reactions. documents.text: 固定入力から実行・検証 Sod衝撃波管：Godunov型更新と自己相似解 Sod衝撃波管を自己相似Riemann解と比べ、密度誤差の減少・正値性・境界流束を含む収支を確認する。 γ=1.4、左右(ρ,u,p)=(1,0,1)/(0.125,0,0.1)、初期不連続x=0.5、t=0.2の標準問題。80/160セルの区分一定Godunov型＋HLLC＋SSPRK3を自己相似Euler解と比較する。 式・図・誤差の解説 · 対応するコードZIP 前提理想気体、1次元一様格子、正の密度・圧力、CFL=0.3。名付き標準問題の物理定義はJSONに明示し、異なる定義は拒否する。参照の圧力は既存exact_eulerの区間二分法で評価する。Godunov原報の厳密Riemann一段更新そのものではない。単位密度・速度・圧力・長さ・時間は無次元。エネルギーはE=p/(γ−1)+ρu²/2。境界・モデルの範囲両端は端値外挿。波が端へ達しないt≤0.2を対象に、総量変化からT(F_left−F_right)を引く。初速0でも圧力差により全運動量は変化する。 入力と実行 固定入力 / recipes/sod.json 実行する場所：atlas-code-2026-11-22（ZIPを展開した中の配布版フォルダ） python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python run_recipe.py --input recipes/sod.json --output output-sodテストと依存関係のファイルpython -m pytest -q tests/test_recipes.py core / requirements.txt testing / requirements.txt plotting / requirements.txt 出力・検証条件・引用を確認する できるファイルと参照出力 result.json (JSON) · 配布版の参照出力 solution.csv (CSV) · 配布版の参照出力 参照の種類と比較方法 細格子160セルの各中心でρ,u,pと同位置・同時刻の参照値を併記。初期値も点サンプルをセル値として与える既存solverを使う。解析的な波構造を使うが、圧力根の数値評価を含み、別コードベースとの独立照合ではない。 同梱された参照出力の代表値 固定入力の参照出力から表示しています。有限格子の値と解析解・独立参照を区別し、再実行の判定には下の許容誤差表を使います。 1e-08/metrics/minimum_pressure 遠方の物理境界流束を差し引いた相対収支誤差。value ≤ 1e-10/metrics/physical_boundary_balance_relative_defect 指定した終端時刻まで進んだ。value ≤ 1e-14/metrics/final_time_error 全数値条件の判定all values = true/checks 実行した固定入力のSHA-256value = 45fe724864902d9314398b9a41c7300651a624570390dcbb505295c4cb46141f/input_sha256 入力に記載した条件の合格value = true/passed 失敗・未収束と確認の限界 2026-11-22. https://hrkoyama.github.io/numerical-methods-atlas/code-and-data/?lang=en#sod-en 計算に使った設定・変更・ハッシュ・参照日を追記してください。手法を研究に使うときは、以下の原論文も確認し引用します。 self-similar Riemann solution; check decreasing density error, positivity and boundary-flux balances. Standard γ=1.4 Sod tube with left/right (ρ,u,p)=(1,0,1)/(0.125,0,0.1), initial jump x=0.5 and t=0.2. Compare 80/160-cell piecewise-constant Godunov-type/HLLC/SSPRK3 updates with a self-similar Euler solution. The named benchmark's physical definition is explicit in JSON; incompatible definitions are rejected. Reference pressure is evaluated by the existing exact_euler bracketed bisection. This is not the original exact-Riemann one-step Godunov algorithm.UnitsDensity, velocity, pressure, length and time are nondimensional. Energy is E=p/(γ−1)+ρu²/2.Boundaries and model scopeEdge-extrapolated boundaries. For t≤0.2, before the wave fan reaches the ends, subtract T(F_left−F_right) from integral changes. Unequal pressures cause a nonzero total-momentum change despite zero initial velocity. 前提単位密度、[0,2π)²、ν=0.1、T=0.5。u₀=sin x cos y、v₀=−cos x sin y。既存ソルバーの移流・拡散安定性に基づくCFL=0.2、時間感度検査は0.1。単位無次元。速度振幅1、座標周期2π、粘性νの次元は長さ²/時間。圧力は単位密度での比圧力。平均運動エネルギーは〈u²+v²〉/2。境界・モデルの範囲2方向周期、圧力平均0。u・vは異なるMAC面、圧力はセル中心。Poissonは連続k²ではなく離散DG記号を逆演算。 入力と実行 固定入力 / recipes/taylor-green.json 実行する場所：atlas-code-2026-11-22（ZIPを展開した中の配布版フォルダ） python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python run_recipe.py --input recipes/taylor-green.json --output documents.title: A-stability, L-stability and error norms · An Atlas of Numerical Methods
documents.text: ← Reading chapters IN THIS EDITION THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data A-stability, L-stability and error norms A-stability and L-stability describe the response of a time integrator to linear decay modes. L1, L2 and L∞ instead describe the size and distribution of an error. They answer different questions. A method can be stable with a large error, and a small algebraic residual need not imply a small PDE error. A/L-stability classification and accurate wave amplitudes and speeds are separate questions. For reading the magnitude and argument of an amplification factor, see von Neumann analysis: dissipation and dispersion basics. A-stability concerns the whole left half-plane# Apply a one-step method to y′=λy, with z=λΔt. Its stability function satisfies yn+1=R(z)yn,S={z∈C:∣R(z)∣≤1}.yn+1​=R(z)yn​,S={z∈C:∣R(z)∣≤1}. The method is A-stable if its absolute-stability region contains the entire closed left half-plane. In particular, R must have no pole there. Thus a scalar mode with Re λ≤0 does not grow for any positive step size in this test. Dahlquist (1963) is a foundational A-stability reference in the linear-multistep setting. The one-step notation here is used to make the comparison transparent. Forward Euler, R(z)=1+z, is stable on the negative real axis only for −2≤z≤0. No consistent explicit RK method is A-stable: its nonconstant stability polynomial is unbounded along the negative real axis. Being implicit alone does not guarantee A-stability. L-stability also damps infinitely stiff modes# An L-stable one-step method is A-stable and satisfies lim⁡∣z∣→∞, Re⁡z<0R(z)=0.∣z∣→∞,Rez<0lim​R(z)=0. This extra property damps modes that are much faster than the chosen step. Backward Euler has R(z)=1/(1−z), so it is both A-stable and L-stable. Crank–Nicolson / the trapezoidal rule has RCN(z)=1+z/21−z/2,lim⁡z→−∞RCN(z)=−1.RCN​(z)=1−z/21+z/2​,z→−∞lim​RCN​(z)=−1. It is A-stable but not L-stable: very stiff negative-real modes alternate sign and decay only slowly. Implicit midpoint has the same scalar linear R(z), although its nonlinear update is different from the trapezoidal rule. For z=−1000, backward Euler gives about 0.001 in one step, while CN gives about −0.996; the exact factor is exp(−1000). For the implemented SDIRK2, γ=1−1/2,R(z)=1+(1−2γ)z(1−γz)2.γ=1−1/2​,R(z)=(1−γz)21+(1−2γ)z​. Its poles are in the right half-plane, it is A-stable and its large-z limit is zero. This is the L-stable two-stage family associated with Alexander (1977). BDF2 is a two-step method: analyze its characteristic roots and parasitic mode, rather than assigning it an arbitrary single-valued R(z). These are linear absolute-stability statements. Accuracy, nonlinear contractivity, SSP/TVD inheritance, positivity and boundary stability require their own checks. Eigenvalues alone can also miss transient growth of nonnormal operators. An A-stable time step cannot repair an inconsistent spatial discretization, and L-stability cannot make an underresolved transient accurate. Continuous L1, L2 and L∞ errors# For scalar error e(x)=u_h(x)−u_ref(x) on a domain Ω, ∥e∥L1=∫Ω∣e∣ dV,∥e∥L2=(∫Ω∣e∣2 dV)1/2,∥e∥L∞=ess sup⁡x∈Ω∣e(x)∣.∥e∥L1​=∫Ω​∣e∣dV,∥e∥L2​=(∫Ω​∣e∣2dV)1/2,∥e∥L∞​=x∈Ωesssup​∣e(x)∣. L1 measures integrated absolute error. L2 emphasizes larger deviations more strongly. L∞ measures the worst error apart from measure-zero sets. For a continuous error on a compact domain, the essential supremum equals the maximum. For discontinuous solutions, the value assigned exactly at a jump does not change the continuous norm. For a domain with volume V, mean absolute error is L1/V and RMS error is L2/√V. These normalized quantities have the same physical units as u; unnormalized integral norms also contain powers of length. State the convention before comparing domains of different size. Discrete weights and the reference representation# For finite-volume error e_i between a numerical cell mean and a reference cell mean, with positive cell volumes V_i, E1=∑iVi∣ei∣,E2=(∑iVi∣ei∣2)1/2,E∞=max⁡i∣ei∣.E1​=i∑​Vi​∣ei​∣,E2​=(i∑​Vi​∣ei​∣2)1/2,E∞​=imax​∣ei​∣. On a uniform grid, V_i=h^d. On the unit interval, these become mean absolute error, RMS error and maximum cell-mean error. On a nonuniform mesh, an unweighted arithmetic mean generally gives the wrong spatial weighting. For e=(1,3) and cell volumes (0.75,0.25), E1=1.5, E2=√3 and E∞=3; unweighted means disagree. The Euclidean vector norm np.linalg.norm(e) omits the h^(d/2) factor of a physical discrete L2 norm. Comparing that raw norm across meshes can therefore change an apparent convergence exponent. Relative error E_p/||u_ref||_p needs a stated reference norm; when the denominator is zero, it is undefined. Any regularization must be explicitly reported. A reference at cell centers is not an exact cell-average reference. DG and FEM need reconstruction and quadrature inside elements; a coefficient-vector norm is not automatically a function L2 norm. Likewise, a maximum over sample points is a sampled L∞ diagnostic, not necessarily the exact supremum of a high-order reconstructed field. Vector components with different units should be reported separately or nondimensionalized with stated scales. Convergence, shocks and algebraic residuals# For matched runs at the same physical time and error convention, the observed order is pobs=log⁡(Ecoarse/Efine)log⁡(hcoarse/hfine).pobs​=log(hcoarse​/hfine​)log(Ecoarse​/Efine​)​. Temporal error, reference error, quadrature error, roundoff and incomplete iterative convergence can mask spatial order. Refine time separately, or state how Δt scales with h. Adaptive ODE tolerance is a local, component-scaled error control; it is not a global spatial L2 error bound. Different norms can behave differently near shocks. For example, an O(1) error supported on width O(h) has L1=O(h), L2=O(√h) and L∞=O(1). This simple scaling is not a universal convergence-rate claim for a shock solver. A useful L1 refinement result need not imply maximum-norm convergence of a shifted jump. For Ax=b, the residual is r=b−Ax. The solution error satisfies x_num−x_exact=−A^(−1)r, so conditioning matters. An algebraic residual compares against the discrete equation; discretization error compares that equation's solution against the continuous problem. See sparse/nonlinear solvers and the Lax–Richtmyer discussion. Where the atlas reports each quantity# The equation gallery reports L1/MAE, L2/RMS and L∞ over its stored unit-interval profiles. Its labels retain the distinction between exact cell means, point-sampled Euler references and absent references. The browser stability laboratory has a point-sampled L1/MAE diagnostic and amplification factors; it does not thereby measure a reconstructed finite-volume function norm. P1 FEM integrates L2 and H1 seminorm errors inside triangles. Periodic MAC flow reports a combined velocity RMS error and maximum absolute discrete divergence. These are different diagnostics. Stiff integration reports maximum error over accepted time nodes, separate from nonlinear stage residuals and local step estimates. Original exhibits keep their documented conventions; this chapter does not retroactively relabel point samples as cell averages or certify a missing maximum-norm calculation. documents.title: Adjoint methods and inverse problems | Numerical Methods Atlas
documents.text: Adjoint methods and inverse problems Adjoints efficiently compute sensitivities when state and parameter dimensions are large but there are few objectives. Obtaining a gradient does not establish uniqueness of an inverse problem. Problem and representative equations For a discrete state equation R(u,m)=0 and scalar objective J, define L=J−λᵀR. With suitable invertibility of R_u, solve R_uᵀλ=J_uᵀ to avoid explicit state sensitivities for every parameter. Subscripts denote partial derivatives; the signs follow this Lagrangian convention. RuTλ=JuT,dJdm=Jm−λTRm.RuT​λ=JuT​,dmdJ​=Jm​−λTRm​. Algorithm Solve the forward state, solve the adjoint using residual/objective derivatives, then assemble the gradient. Transient problems need forward-state history and a storage/recomputation strategy. Discretizing a continuous adjoint and differentiating a discretization need not agree on a finite mesh. Conditions and pitfalls Differentiate boundary conditions, mesh/coordinate dependence, observations and regularization consistently. Nonsmooth limiters and moving shocks challenge ordinary differentiability assumptions. Incomplete forward or adjoint convergence contaminates gradients. What to check Use directional Taylor tests: J(m+hv)−J(m)−h∇J·v should behave as O(h²) in a smooth, sufficiently converged regime. Add adjoint inner-product and finite-difference tests. Assess identifiability, regularization and data error separately for the inverse problem. Publication scope and related entries Reading, representative equations and sources are published. Dedicated code and numerical verification remain planned. The suggested checks above are not measured results, and code/results of other methods are not presented as validation of this method. documents.title: Advanced limiters: TVB and positivity preservation · An Atlas of Numerical Methods
documents.text: ← Reading chapters IN THIS EDITION THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Advanced limiters: TVB and positivity preservation The limiter notebook includes a TVB scalar experiment and a separate conservative Euler-state scaling demonstration. These address different failure modes: loss of accuracy near a smooth extremum and inadmissible thermodynamic states. TVB modified minmod# For a candidate increment v and neighboring increments a and b, define m~(v,a,b)={v,∣v∣≤MΔx2,m(v,a,b),otherwise,m(v,a,b)={v,m(v,a,b),​∣v∣≤MΔx2,otherwise,​ where m is the generalized minmod: the smallest magnitude with a shared sign, and zero when signs disagree. Our scalar demonstration chooses v=(a+b)/2. At M=0 this reduces to the two-increment minmod used in the TVD experiment. At M>0 sufficiently small increments survive even when the neighboring slopes have opposite signs, permitting a smooth peak to remain curved. The dx-squared threshold reflects the scale of smooth-extremum face deviations in the RKDG setting. Its coefficient has units of solution divided by length squared; it is not a universal dimensionless constant. Rescaling the dependent variable or coordinates requires reconsidering M. Increments and derivatives require different thresholds. Cockburn and Shu (1989) develop the TVB RKDG framework. This edition implements the modified-minmod building block in scalar finite volumes, rather than that full RKDG method or its theorem. The notebook computes M=0,10,50 on both the sine and square pulse. Compare errors and measured maximum TV: allowing small extrema means TV need not decrease at every step, and a large M can also admit small oscillations beside a discontinuity. Changing M does not prove a uniform TVB bound for an arbitrary method. No Euler-system TVB extension is implemented. Positive density and pressure are different constraints# For ideal-gas conservative variables U=(rho,m,E), p(U)=(γ−1)(E−∣m∣22ρ),G={U:ρ>0, p(U)>0}.p(U)=(γ−1)(E−2ρ∣m∣2​),G={U:ρ>0, p(U)>0}. Positive density alone does not ensure positive internal energy. TVD, TVB, an entropy fix, and the absence of visible wiggles do not automatically make Euler states admissible. A negative pressure can arise from excessive kinetic energy even when rho and E are positive. A mean-preserving scaling building block# Start with an admissible conservative cell average Ubar. Scale every supplied reconstruction point by the same factor: U^α=Uˉ+θ(Uα−Uˉ),0≤θ≤1.Uα​=Uˉ+θ(Uα​−Uˉ),0≤θ≤1. If the original points have quadrature mean Ubar, the scaled points retain it. Using a single theta across components and points is essential to this particular construction. Clipping rho, pressure, or total energy independently does not have that conservation property. First bound theta by the minimum reconstructed density: θρ=min⁡(1,ρˉ−ϵρρˉ−ρmin⁡)if ρmin⁡<ϵρ;θρ=1 otherwise.θρ​=min(1,ρˉ​−ρmin​ρˉ​−ϵρ​​)if ρmin​<ϵρ​;θρ​=1 otherwise. Then shrink theta in [0,theta_rho] until every supplied point also satisfies p(Uhat) ≥ epsilon_p. Ideal-gas pressure is concave for positive density, so the admissible part of this line segment contains the mean and can be found by bisection. The implementation uses 64 iterations and a small roundoff retreat. Density and pressure floors are input parameters, not inserted mass or energy. Inadmissible averages raise an error; scaling around a bad mean cannot repair conservation and positivity together in this way. This follows the convex-scaling idea of Zhang and Shu (2010), with a deliberately simple common-state scaling and numerical pressure search. It is not a line-by-line reproduction of their two-stage density-polynomial and state limiter. The implementation covers the supplied points only; arbitrary polynomial values between those points are not automatically bounded. What the demonstration actually verifies# The three-node cell has xi=-1,0,1, positive Gauss–Lobatto weights (1/6,2/3,1/6), gamma=1.4, and Ubar=(1,0,2.5). The raw states are Ubar + xi times delta. Choose delta=(1.2,0,0) for a density violation, (0,3,0) for a pressure violation, or (1.2,3,1) for a combined violation. Their weighted mean is exactly Ubar in real arithmetic. The plot samples only these three nodes and reports theta, minimum limited density, minimum limited pressure, and the conservative mean defect, with epsilon_rho=epsilon_p=1e-8. These are constructed reconstruction tests, not blast-wave or rarefaction time integrations. import numpy as np from numart.limiters import positive_reconstruction mean = np.array([1., 0., 2.5]) raw = mean + np.array([-1., 0., 1.])[:, None] * [0., 3., 0.] limited, theta = positive_reconstruction(mean, raw) Tests check that an already admissible reconstruction is unchanged, bad means are rejected, and both floors and conservative quadrature means survive the three failure cases. From reconstruction to a fully discrete guarantee# A complete positivity-preserving Euler method also needs a compatible positivity-preserving numerical flux, positive quadrature decomposition including interface states, a corresponding wave-speed/CFL restriction, and limiting at all required stages. SSP time stepping propagates a forward-Euler positivity property only when that property and its step restriction already hold. Source terms and boundary treatment require their own checks. This helper is not wired into the existing Euler MUSCL, finite-difference WENO, CT/GLM, or KEEP time updates. Those solvers retain their documented limitations. A future complete implementation should add stage-by-stage admissibility and conservation checks, near-vacuum double rarefaction, and strong blast-wave tests before claiming positivity preservation over time. Multidimensional and non-ideal-EOS extensions need additional analysis. Historical atlas →Computed gallery → ON THIS PAGE

documents.title: Preconditioning, dual time stepping, and residual distribution · An Atlas of Numerical Methods
documents.text: ← Reading chapters IN THIS EDITION THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Preconditioning, dual time stepping, and residual distribution Condition numbers and PDE preconditioning# For Ax=b, the 2-norm condition number is κ₂(A)=σmax/σmin. It measures sensitivity to perturbations rather than the convergence rate of a particular iteration. Left preconditioning gives P^{-1}Ax=P^{-1}b; right preconditioning gives AP^{-1}y=b, x=P^{-1}y. For symmetric positive-definite systems, P^{-1/2}AP^{-1/2} supports symmetry-preserving comparisons. conditioning_example constructs A=S B S, where B is a 1D Poisson matrix and S is diagonal scaling. It demonstrates the change in condition number under symmetric Jacobi scaling. It does not implement Turkel's low-Mach flow preconditioning matrix. Compressible PDEs pose a separate preconditioning problem when low-Mach convective and acoustic characteristic speeds differ greatly. A pseudo-time system such as Γ(U) ∂U/∂τ + R(U)=0 modifies characteristic speeds, convergence, and numerical dissipation. Deriving Γ, transforming variables, choosing Mach-dependent coefficients, and maintaining boundary consistency require additional verification. Replacing the physical time derivative indiscriminately changes the time-dependent solution. Turkel (1987). Dual time stepping# Applying BDF2 in physical time to dU/dt+R(U)=0 gives 3Un+1−4Un+Un−12Δt+R(Un+1)=0.2Δt3Un+1−4Un+Un−1​+R(Un+1)=0. At each physical step, evolve the pseudo-time equation for Q, dQdτ+3Q−4Un+Un−12Δt+R(Q)=0,dτdQ​+2Δt3Q−4Un+Un−1​+R(Q)=0, to a steady state. Backward Euler starts the first step. Physical-time accuracy depends on Δt, spatial error, and incomplete inner convergence. A large physical CFL alone does not establish accurate time evolution. Jameson (1991). dual_time_advection is a minimal periodic 1D example: implicit upwind advection with BDF1/BDF2, solved by a Jacobi pseudo-time iteration. The inner residual threshold is tol*max(1,||b||∞), with default tol=1e-10. Failure to converge within the iteration limit raises an error. Tests compare against an independent dense solve of the BDF2 discrete equations. This is a reduced model rather than Jameson's complete compressible-flow multigrid algorithm. Residual distribution schemes# Distribute an element residual Φ_K=∫K ∇·F(U) dV to its nodes while preserving Σ_{i∈K} Φ_i^K=Φ_K. This conservation condition connects continuous finite elements with upwind ideas. Abgrall (2006), author-hosted review. rd_residual is a minimal 1D P1 scalar-advection example. It assigns all of Φ_K=a(u_{i+1}-u_i) to the downstream node and divides by lumped mass h. Tests establish equivalence to first-order upwind differences in this case. 2D triangular N/LDA schemes, nonlinear blending, time-consistent mass matrices, and Euler systems remain unimplemented. Roe, entropy fixes, Einfeldt, and rotated solvers# Roe uses a linearization satisfying F_R-F_L=Ã(U_R-U_L) and its eigensystem. This edition forms sqrt(ρ)-weighted u and H, with ã²=(γ-1)(H̃-ũ²/2), and adds dissipation through wave strengths and eigenvectors. Roe (1981). The entropy fix replaces the absolute acoustic eigenvalue below δ with (λ²+δ²)/(2δ). HLLE is a separate flux using Einfeldt-type left/right wave speeds for strong low-density expansions. Roe entropy correction, HLLE positivity properties, and carbuncle treatments address different problems. Einfeldt (1988), Einfeldt et al. (1991). Rotated-hybrid Riemann solvers combine fluxes using directions beyond the face normal to balance shock robustness and shear-layer resolution. A coordinate rotation alone does not reproduce this construction. This edition adds a specified directional HLLE/Roe composition and cylinder-forebody tests. This explicit two-flux experiment is distinct from an optimized reproduction of the original Rotated-RHLL dissipation formula. Nishikawa–Kitamura (2008). Roe's Property U# Roe's 1981 paper, author-uploaded full text, pp. 359–360 uses four conditions: (i) a linear mapping from conserved-state space to flux space for each fixed state pair; (ii) the coincident-state limit equals the physical Jacobian; (iii) the matrix maps the state jump exactly onto the flux jump; (iv) its eigenvectors are linearly independent. The two-state matrix need not depend linearly on its arguments. For physical ideal-gas Euler states the construction below also has real acoustic/contact speeds. Here is the algebra implemented and independently checked in this atlas. For U=(ρ,ρu,E), H=(E+p)/ρ, set z=√ρ(1,u,H). Then U(z)=(z12z1z2(z1z3+(γ−1)z22/2)/γ),F(z)=(z1z2((γ+1)z22/2+(γ−1)z1z3)/γz2z3).U(z)=​z12​z1​z2​(z1​z3​+(γ−1)z22​/2)/γ​​,F(z)=​z1​z2​((γ+1)z22​/2+(γ−1)z1​z3​)/γz2​z3​​​. Both maps are quadratic. Their midpoint Jacobians B=∂U/∂z and C=∂F/∂z therefore satisfy ΔU=B(z̄)Δz and ΔF=C(z̄)Δz exactly. Consequently Ã=C(z̄)B(z̄)⁻¹ has the jump property. Ratios of z̄ give u~=ρLuL+ρRuRρL+ρR,H~=ρLHL+ρRHRρL+ρR,c~2=(γ−1)(H~−u~2/2).u=ρL​​+ρR​​ρL​​uL​+ρR​​uR​​,H=ρL​​+ρR​​ρL​​HL​+ρR​​HR​​,c2=(γ−1)(H−u2/2). At equal states, the chain rule gives CB⁻¹=∂F/∂U. The independently constructed eigenbasis has speeds ũ−c̃,ũ,ũ+c̃. Since c̃>0, its three eigenvectors span the state space. We check the parameter-vector matrix against this eigenbasis, the analytic Jacobian, and 2000 deterministic physical state pairs. If ΔF=sΔU for a single nonzero Rankine–Hugoniot jump, then ÃΔU=sΔU: the jump lies in the speed-s eigenspace. The unmodified Roe flux consequently recognizes isolated contact/shock jumps. This does not make every reconstructed, time-discretized shock calculation exact. Smoothing |λ| changes the flux without changing the matrix identity, and can smear a stationary shock. An expansion discontinuity can also satisfy the jump relation. Our reversed stationary normal-shock pair passes Property U but the raw Roe flux differs from the entropy Riemann reference. This is a numerical counterexample to confusing the jump property with entropy selection. The entropy fix is an additional design choice; neither gives a multidimensional carbuncle guarantee. python scripts/build_shock_robustness.py saves the matrix checks, moving and stationary shocks, a contact and the expansion counterexample in the diagnostic manifest. Rotated Riemann sources: Ren (2003), Roe–Nishikawa et al. (2005), Nishikawa–Kitamura (2008) and the atlas experiment Preconditioning matrices, sonic points and entropy fixes · Damping Runge–Kutta iterations for steady solutions Historical atlas →Computed gallery → ON THIS PAGE

documents.title: Arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian methods · An Atlas of Numerical Methods
documents.text: ← Reading chapters IN THIS EDITION THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian methods Eulerian cells stay fixed while fluid crosses their faces. Lagrangian cells move with the fluid. In ALE, the mesh velocity w can be chosen independently of the fluid velocity u. Hirt, Amsden, and Cook (1974) provide a classical all-speed ALE formulation. The flux is relative to the moving face# Reynolds transport gives, for a moving control volume K(t), ddt∫K(t)U dV+∫∂K(t)[F(U)⋅n−(w⋅n)U]dS=0.dtd​∫K(t)​UdV+∫∂K(t)​[F(U)⋅n−(w⋅n)U]dS=0. With w = 0 this is Eulerian. Choosing the normal mesh speed equal to the fluid normal speed gives the Lagrangian mass-flux limit. Pressure still transfers momentum and energy across a material face; setting mass flux to zero does not set every Euler flux to zero. Geometry must obey a conservation law too# For a uniform state to remain uniform, changing cell volumes and face motion must agree: d∣K∣dt=∫∂Kw⋅n dS.dtd∣K∣​=∫∂K​w⋅ndS. Its discrete counterpart is the geometric conservation law (GCL). A mesh-motion routine and a flow update that use inconsistent swept volumes can create a spurious flow from constant data, even if each looks accurate separately. A reproducible one-step check# numart.geometry.moving_volume_uniform_test deforms faces on [0,1] by a smooth sinusoidal displacement with fixed endpoints. Face velocity is the actual displacement divided by delta t. For constant scalar q, it updates the extensive quantity Vq with relative flux (a−w)q and divides by the new volume. The same displacement appears in both operations. import numpy as np from numart.geometry import moving_volume_uniform_test old_faces, new_faces, q = moving_volume_uniform_test(phase=0.8) print(np.max(np.abs(q - 1))) Uniform-state preservation is checked to roundoff over several deformation phases. The amplitude restriction ensures positive cell widths. This is a 1D moving-volume identity check, not an ALE Euler solver or a test of accuracy for nonuniform data. Mesh motion, remapping, and distortion# A complete ALE method may move vertices, solve a Lagrangian or relative-flux step, and remap to a better mesh. Conservative remapping, mesh tangling, boundary motion, and temporal consistency require additional tests. A remap that preserves total mass can still violate positivity or fail to preserve a constant state. Use the mesh chapter to separate topology from motion, and the coordinate chapter to distinguish moving control volumes from changing tensor bases. Neither replacing x by r nor moving plotted vertices automatically constructs an ALE method. Historical atlas →Computed gallery → ON THIS PAGE

documents.title: Algebraic multigrid / AMG | Numerical Methods Atlas
documents.text: Algebraic multigrid / AMG AMG constructs a multilevel hierarchy and interpolation from a matrix. Smooth error means error that relaxation removes poorly, rather than only geometrically long-wavelength error. Problem and representative equations For Au=b, use residual r=b−Au, restriction R and interpolation P. The Galerkin coarse operator is A_c=RAP. Correct the fine approximation using a coarse residual solve. The inverse in the formula expresses the principle; a multilevel cycle normally approximates that solve recursively. Ac=RAP,r=b−Au,u←u+PAc−1Rr.Ac​=RAP,r=b−Au,u←u+PAc−1​Rr. Algorithm A cycle applies pre-relaxation, computes/restricts the residual, corrects on the coarse space and post-relaxes. Classical AMG uses strength connections and C/F splitting; aggregation variants group unknowns. Near-nullspace information, such as rigid motions for elasticity, must be represented by interpolation. Conditions and pitfalls Success on a scalar elliptic problem does not ensure robustness for nonsymmetric advection, saddle points or strong anisotropy. CG preconditioning requires compatible symmetry/positive-definiteness properties. A pure-Neumann problem still has a constant nullspace and a right-hand-side compatibility condition. What to check Use manufactured Poisson solutions while varying mesh size and coefficient contrast. Measure true residuals, solution errors and per-cycle reduction; record hierarchy sizes and nonzero counts. Few iterations do not establish small discretization error. documents.title: Automatic differentiation | Numerical Methods Atlas
documents.text: Automatic differentiation Automatic differentiation applies the chain rule to elementary operations in a program. It is distinct from symbolic manipulation and from finite-difference differentiation with a chosen step. Problem and representative equations For z=φ(x), forward mode propagates ż=φ_x ẋ; reverse mode accumulates φ_xᵀz̄ into x̄. Floating-point rounding remains, so derivatives are not literally error-free, but there is no finite-difference truncation step. z˙=∂ϕ∂xx˙,xˉ+=(∂ϕ∂x)Tzˉ,wT(Jv)=vT(JTw).z˙=∂x∂ϕ​x˙,xˉ+=(∂x∂ϕ​)Tzˉ,wT(Jv)=vT(JTw). Algorithm Decompose the computation into elementary operations and store values with tangents or the history needed for reverse accumulation. Few input directions favor forward mode; a scalar output with many inputs favors reverse mode. Distinguish differentiating solver iterations from implicitly differentiating the converged solution. Conditions and pitfalls Branches differentiate the executed path. Check nondifferentiability and conventions for abs, max, limiters, contacts and events. Audit stop-gradient, external primitives and iterative stopping. AD is not a guarantee of a classical derivative of every discontinuous bit-level operation. What to check Test analytic elementary cases, directional Taylor remainders and the duality identity wᵀ(Jv)=vᵀ(Jᵀw). Avoid finite-difference steps so small that rounding dominates. Include boundary and parameter dependence when differentiating PDE residuals. Publication scope and related entries Reading, representative equations and sources are published. Dedicated code and numerical verification remain planned. The suggested checks above are not measured results, and code/results of other methods are not presented as validation of this method. documents.title: Orthogonal polynomials and mesh basis functions | Numerical Methods Atlas
documents.text: Orthogonal polynomials and mesh basis functions A mesh supplies cells, geometry and connectivity. A basis supplies the functions used to represent a field on those cells. The choice of basis is separate from cell shape and variable staggering. The basis notebook makes modes, nodes and their mass matrices visible. The existing DG advection example already uses Legendre modes internally; this chapter exposes the algebra behind it. Start on a reference element# Map a physical interval of length h and center x_c to a reference interval: x=xc+Jξ,J=h/2,−1≤ξ≤1,uh(x)=∑j=0pajϕj(ξ).x=xc​+Jξ,J=h/2,−1≤ξ≤1,uh​(x)=j=0∑p​aj​ϕj​(ξ). The p+1 coefficients are element degrees of freedom. In a continuous finite-element method, neighboring elements share selected boundary degrees of freedom. DG keeps independent element coefficients and couples traces through numerical fluxes. A local polynomial basis can serve either formulation. For constant material coefficients and an affine map, the element mass and diffusion matrices are Mij=J∫−11ϕiϕj dξ,Kij=J−1∫−11ϕi′ϕj′ dξ.Mij​=J∫−11​ϕi​ϕj​dξ,Kij​=J−1∫−11​ϕi′​ϕj′​dξ. Curved maps introduce a variable Jacobian; variable density or coefficients also change these integrals. Reference-element orthogonality alone then does not make the physical matrix diagonal. Legendre modes and orthonormal modes# With unit weight on [-1,1], the Legendre family satisfies P0=1,P1=ξ,P2=(3ξ2−1)/2,(n+1)Pn+1=(2n+1)ξPn−nPn−1,P0​=1,P1​=ξ,P2​=(3ξ2−1)/2,(n+1)Pn+1​=(2n+1)ξPn​−nPn−1​, ∫−11PiPj dξ=22i+1δij,P^i=2i+12Pi.∫−11​Pi​Pj​dξ=2i+12​δij​,Pi​=22i+1​​Pi​. The ordinary Legendre mass is diagonal, with unequal diagonal entries. The orthonormal reference mass is the identity. Their coefficient values differ, although both span exactly the same degree-p polynomial space. The constant mode encodes the element mean; the higher Legendre modes have zero mean. See NIST DLMF §18.3 for normalization and §18.9 for recurrence relations. Nodal Lagrange functions represent the same space# Choose distinct nodes and define cardinal polynomials: ℓj(ξ)=∏k≠jξ−ξkξj−ξk,ℓj(ξi)=δij,uh=∑jujℓj.ℓj​(ξ)=k=j∏​ξj​−ξk​ξ−ξk​​,ℓj​(ξi​)=δij​,uh​=j∑​uj​ℓj​. Here the coefficients u_j are nodal values. In a modal expansion, the coefficients are polynomial amplitudes. For the same polynomial, the change of representation is ui=∑jVijaj,Vij=Pj(ξi),a=V−1u.ui​=j∑​Vij​aj​,Vij​=Pj​(ξi​),a=V−1u. The notebook compares equispaced nodes and Gauss–Lobatto–Legendre (GLL) nodes. It reports the condition number of this Legendre Vandermonde; that number depends on normalization and is not the condition number of a complete PDE solve. Endpoint clustering can help interpolation, but does not remove Gibbs oscillations at a jump. Quadrature and the diagonal-mass caveat# With p+1 points, Gauss–Legendre quadrature integrates polynomials through degree 2p+1. GLL includes the endpoints and integrates through degree 2p−1. Its interior points are the zeros of P'_p, and its weights are wi=2p(p+1)Pp(ξi)2,p≥1.wi​=p(p+1)Pp​(ξi​)22​,p≥1. Products of degree-p basis functions can have degree 2p. Consequently, GLL collocation gives a quadrature mass diag(w), while the exactly integrated GLL nodal mass generally has off-diagonal entries. On an affine interval with unit weight, their difference is rank one. The highest Legendre squared norm is 2/p under GLL quadrature, instead of 2/(2p+1). The notebook lets you switch between both matrices. These facts, and an efficient correction, are derived in Teukolsky's mass-matrix note. For constant-coefficient stiffness, the polynomial degree is at most 2p−2, so the same GLL rule is sufficient. Nonlinear fluxes and variable metrics can require additional quadrature or a suitable split formulation; a diagonal mass alone is not a nonlinear stability guarantee. DLMF §3.5 explains Gaussian quadrature more generally. Projection is different from interpolation# An unweighted L2 Legendre projection uses integral moments: ak=2k+12∫−11f(ξ)Pk(ξ) dξ.ak​=22k+1​∫−11​f(ξ)Pk​(ξ)dξ. Nodal interpolation instead matches f at the chosen nodes. They agree for every polynomial of degree at most p, but need not agree for other functions. For exp(ξ), the notebook shows rapidly decreasing errors as p increases. For sign(ξ), the displayed overshoot and slow convergence expose the loss of smoothness; neither approximation supplies a shock limiter. The jump is integrated on two separate half-intervals, and interpolation explicitly uses sign(0)=0. L2 errors are integrated with 80-point Gauss rules on each half. Quadrilaterals and triangles have different polynomial spaces# On a quadrilateral, a tensor basis takes products of one-dimensional functions: ϕij(ξ,η)=ℓi(ξ)ℓj(η),0≤i,j≤p.ϕij​(ξ,η)=ℓi​(ξ)ℓj​(η),0≤i,j≤p. This Q_p space has (p+1)^2 functions. A triangle's total-degree P_p space has (p+1)(p+2)/2. Thus Q2 has nine degrees of freedom, while triangular P2 has six. The cell topology determines which reference map and trace connectivity are needed. DefElement's Lagrange definition distinguishes these spaces and nodal variants. On the reference triangle (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), barycentric coordinates are λ0=1−ξ−η, λ1=ξ, λ2=η. The P1 vertex functions are λ_i. P2 has vertex functions λ_i(2λ_i−1) and edge functions 4λ_iλ_j. They form a partition of unity and reproduce quadratic fields; they are not an orthogonal basis. The notebook colors each of these six shape functions on the actual triangle. Orthogonal modal triangle bases can instead be built from suitably weighted Jacobi polynomials in collapsed coordinates, including the Dubiner (1991) construction. A rectangular Legendre tensor product restricted to a triangle does not automatically retain orthogonality. This edition implements P1/P2 nodal triangles and quadrilateral tensor evaluation; a Dubiner implementation remains additional work. Other orthogonal families and their measures# Orthogonality always includes a domain and a weight. Changing either changes the inner product. The notebook also tabulates Chebyshev T modes and demonstrates their nonorthogonality under unit weight. The remaining families below are mathematical reading connections. Conventions follow DLMF §18.2 and §18.3. Chebyshev T_n: T_n(cos θ)=cos(nθ), on [-1,1], weight (1−ξ²)^−1/2. Useful for endpoint-clustered spectral interpolation. They are not mutually orthogonal under the unweighted finite-element mass integral. Jacobi: P_n^(α,β), weight (1−ξ)^α(1+ξ)^β on [-1,1], α,β>−1. This family includes Legendre and, after normalization, Chebyshev; weighted coordinate transforms connect it to simplex bases. Hermite: physicists' H_n has weight exp(−ξ²) on the real line; probabilists' He_n uses exp(−ξ²/2). These are different conventions. Orthogonal Hermite polynomials are distinct from the endpoint value/derivative Hermite interpolation used by CIP. Generalized Laguerre: L_n^(α) uses ξ^α exp(−ξ) on [0,∞), α>−1. It addresses a semi-infinite domain rather than an ordinary bounded mesh cell. Fourier modes: exp(ikx) are orthogonal on a periodic interval with matching integer wave numbers. They form a global periodic basis rather than a mesh-local polynomial family; the spectral advection example uses these modes. Verification and scope# numart.basis supplies Legendre/Chebyshev and nodal tabulation, derivatives, affine interval matrices, GLL quadrature, projection, P1/P2 triangles and tensor products. Tests check continuous Legendre orthogonality, GLL exactness limits, cardinal interpolation, polynomial reproduction, partition of unity, derivative reproduction, the GLL summation-by-parts identity, rank-one mass difference and physical Jacobian scaling. The existing DG solver remains restricted to scalar periodic P0/P1/P2 advection. The published reference-element source is available from the Legendre method record. Saved arrays and source hashes accompany the figure. This adds reference-element building blocks, not a general curved-mesh assembly or a higher-order fluid solver. Continue with mesh connectivity, continuous triangular FEM, DG advection, limiters and variable staggering. Publication scope and related entries Links lead to existing educational code and dated verification records. This reading/translation update changes no scientific code or historical measurements and does not claim reproduction of an entire paper. Legendre modal basis / orthonormal scaling Lagrange nodal basis / GLL collocation Primary publications, supporting sources and review scope Distinguish original research, later variants, author monographs, pedagogical articles and official references. Bibliographic verification differs from consulting selected passages; neither implies a full-paper audit or numerical reproduction. Access-depth notes accompany each source. Saul A. Teukolsky (2015). Short note on the mass matrix for Gauss–Lobatto grid points. Journal of Computational Physics Research publication: proposal or related formulation · Bibliography checked · Consulted record Reviewed as a source for priority-method metadata. The individual method records distinguish reference roles, relevant full-text passages, abstracts and bibliographic checks; this does not imply a new numerical validation. Moshe Dubiner (1991). Spectral methods on triangles and other domains. Journal of Scientific Computing Research publication: proposal or related formulation · Bibliography checked · Consulted record Bibliographic identity checked against the DOI registration on 2026-11-22. Relevant abstracts or selected passages are separately identified in the detailed-reading source notes; this is not a claim of a full-paper audit or numerical reproduction. F. W. J. Olver and A. B. Olde Daalhuis and D. W. Lozier and B. I. Schneider and R. F. Boisvert and C. W. Clark and B. R. Miller and B. V. Saunders and H. S. Cohl and M. A. McClain (eds.) (2010). NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions. Official reference documentation · Selected source passages consulted · Consulted record Living official reference, not the original discovery papers. Sections 3.5 and 18.2/18.3/18.9 supply quadrature and orthogonal-polynomial conventions. The year is initial release, not a claim that the current version dates from 2010. Citation and reuse

documents.title: Benchmark library · An Atlas of Numerical Methods
documents.text: ← Reading chapters IN THIS EDITION THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Benchmark library For the representation behind DG and spectral examples, see orthogonal polynomials and element bases: Legendre modes, nodal transforms, quadrature, and their mass matrices. Each 1D Problem stores the equation, domain, final time, boundaries, initial condition, reference solution, and citation keys. get_problem(name) exposes the same definition to every method. The last array axis contains variables: Euler uses (ρ,ρu,E), shallow water uses (h,hu), and isothermal flow uses (ρ,ρu). Smooth problems# Linear advection uses periodic [0,1], speed a, and initial data sin(2πx). The exact translated solution compares finite differences, DG, and Fourier methods. DG uses modal Legendre P0/P1/P2, upwind boundary fluxes, and SSPRK3. Distinguish the spatial order of Pp from the third-order time integrator. DG has elements × (p+1) unknowns. Fourier integrates the linear modes exactly in time; the gallery does not establish an equal-cost or equal-degree-of-freedom ranking. Nonlinear products, dealiasing, and Gibbs treatments are future work. entropy-wave uses Euler data ρ=1+0.2sin(2πx), u=1,p=1,γ=1.4, periodic [0,1], and t=1. Only density translates, giving an exact reference for smooth accuracy and periodic conservation. Isothermal Euler has no independent energy or entropy variable and does not support this same Euler entropy-wave problem. Shock tubes# Sod: [0,1], x0=0.5, left (ρ,u,p)=(1,0,1), right (0.125,0,0.1), γ=1.4, and t=0.2. Boundaries use zero-gradient extrapolation; the main waves do not reach them before the final time. The exact Riemann solver finds the matching pressure by bisection and samples shocks, contacts, and rarefaction fans. Exact solutions containing a vacuum are unsupported. Sod (1978), exact-solution implementation reference. Lax: [-5,5], x0=0, left (0.445,0.698,3.528), right (0.5,0,0.571), γ=1.4, t=1.3, and extrapolation boundaries. The Lax test and the Lax–Friedrichs algorithm are different namesakes. These are standard parameters from later literature; the original 1954 paper's table has not been directly matched here. Shu–Osher: [-5,5], x0=-4, t=1.8, γ=1.4, left (3.857143,2.629369,10.33333), and right (1+0.2sin(5x),0,1). Ghost states are fixed to the initial conditions evaluated at the domain ends. There is no exact final-time reference; the first-edition figure compares MUSCL and WENO numerical results. Shu–Osher (1989), adopted parameters in Quokka, §3.1.5. Low densities and Einfeldt-type tests# double-rarefaction uses [0,1], x0=0.5, left (1,-2,0.4), right (1,2,0.4), γ=1.4, and t=0.15. This strong expansion is commonly called the 1–2–3 problem. The selected positivity test uses piecewise-constant reconstruction with HLLE. It does not transfer a positivity guarantee to high-order MUSCL or WENO. Einfeldt et al. (1991). Shallow-water and isothermal flow# dam-break solves flat-bottom shallow water with g=1, left h=2, right h=1, u=0, [0,1], and t=0.1. Dry beds, topographic sources, well-balanced discretization, and wetting/drying are unsupported. isothermal uses p=cs²ρ, cs=1, left ρ=1, right ρ=0.125, and u=0 on the same domain and time interval. Both use extrapolation boundaries. First-edition checks compare solvers, admissible states, and conservative form. The reference library now supplies semi-analytic Riemann states and conserved cell means for the equation gallery. The original Problem.reference callbacks for these two cases remain unset; use get_reference for the new evaluations. LeVeque (2002). Riemann fluxes and reconstruction# Rusanov and HLL support Euler, shallow water, and isothermal flow. HLLC, Roe, and HLLE currently support ideal-gas Euler only. HLL uses minimum/maximum local acoustic speeds; HLLE uses Einfeldt-type estimates including Roe averages. Roe applies quadratic entropy smoothing to acoustic eigenvalues with δ=0.1ã, leaving the contact eigenvalue unchanged. This is neither a low-density positivity fix nor a general entropy-stable flux construction. MUSCL uses selectable minmod (default), Superbee, MC, van Leer, or clipped van Albada reconstruction in primitive variables; see limiters. WENO5-JS is a componentwise finite-difference implementation with pointwise fluxes and global LF splitting. A separate reconstruction chapter below adds characteristics and WENO-Z; this original solver remains unchanged. Fully discrete positivity preservation is still future work. A separate advanced limiter exhibit implements TVB modified minmod and positive Euler reconstruction scaling; neither is coupled to these Euler time updates. Errors are labeled pointwise: finite-volume cell averages and finite-difference point values are not strictly interchangeable. See MHD for Orszag–Tang definitions and limits, and elliptic problems for diffusion and Poisson cases. Matching the benchmark to the scheme# The original KEEP exhibit uses a smooth isentropic vortex and conservation diagnostics. Its bare central flux has no shock stabilization and is not presented as a Sod/DMR solver. The movie guide separates those smooth computations from shock-capturing and MHD movies, and keeps steady fields as still images. Equation-first scalar comparisons# The equation gallery adds Burgers and LWR traffic Riemann problems with exact cell-integrated references, plus advection and heat mode tests. It also connects the existing Sod, wet dam-break and isothermal baselines, with each reference convention explicitly labeled. Expanded reconstruction and flux tests# The new reconstruction chapter and interactive comparison add limited parabolic FV, conservative characteristics, FD WENO-Z and an explicit AUSM-family baseline. The original code described above remains a componentwise baseline. Planar shock sensitivity and Roe's Property U have separate verification. Historical atlas →Computed gallery → ON THIS PAGE
